newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa buyers await weaker futures.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa buyers await weaker futures.

text.p: Cocoa consumers in Germany are looking for January/February 1997 cover, but firm sterling versus the mark has nullified the effect of weak futures on outright prices, traders said on Thursday.
Consumers were holding out for price reductions, which could arise if adequate West African new crop supply was confirmed, they added.
December and first quarter cif bean prices of around 2.26-2.29 marks per kg compared with 2.30 marks last week and 2.00 marks a year ago. Buyers' ideas were around 2.20 marks.
London LIFFE cocoa futures were mixed after bouncing from a nine-month low on March of 899 stg. March was at 911 stg, off one, at 1523 GMT.
Traders said chocolate manufacturers had mostly closed their books for the year, which had seen active production but slim profit margins, if any.
"Confectionery output has been up from last year but sales revenues are not matching that," one said.
"All in all, it's been a weak year for manufacturers as well as the trade, with hand-to-mouth buying and little volatility."
But traders did not disagree with a forecast by a confectionery industry association official last week of a three to five percent rise in the German cocoa grind for 1996.
Official figures for the fourth quarter and full year are due for release in the week starting January 13.
Traders remained unimpressed by a series of Ivorian production estimates for 1996/97, which ranged between 850,000 and one million tonnes.
While they said 850,000 tonnes would be bullish, most believed in a result nearer the one million-tonne top end.
The cocoa butter ratio was one point off at 2.68, with implied prices liquid ex-works at 6.32 marks per kg versus 6.40 marks last week.
Sterling was fixed in Frankfurt at 2.5895 marks, compared with 2.5466 marks last Thursday.
